title: Quadratic Models
short: Use parabolas for falling objects and areas, and read the vertex and zeros in context.
trouble: Students report both roots in a time problem, including a negative time that makes no sense.

blocks.html: Parabolas describe many real things: the height of a thrown ball, the area of a fenced pen, the revenue from a price. The vertex answers “how high” or “how much at most,” and the zeros, found with the quadratic formula or factoring, answer “when” or “where.”

Near Earth, gravity pulls a thrown object so that its height is a quadratic in time: $h(t) = -16t^2 + v_0 t + h_0$ in feet, or about $-5t^2 + v_0 t + h_0$ in meters, where $v_0$ is the starting upward speed and $h_0$ the starting height. The negative leading coefficient makes the parabola open down, so the vertex is the highest point. Area problems give quadratics because area multiplies two lengths that both depend on the variable.

blocks.name: graph
blocks.cap: $h(t) = -5t^2 + 20t + 25$: highest at $t = 2$ s ($45$ m), landing at $t = 5$ s. The zero at $t = -1$ is outside the story.

blocks.html: Write the quadratic, then match the question to a feature: maximum or minimum is the vertex; “when is it zero” or “when does it reach a value” is an equation to solve. Keep only answers that make sense in the story.

blocks.title: A launched ball
blocks.q: $h(t) = -5t^2 + 20t + 25$ meters. When does the ball land, and how high does it go?
steps: $t = 5$ or $t = -1$. Negative time is before the launch: it lands at $t = 5$ s.
Highest point: halfway between the zeros, $t = 2$. $h(2) = -20 + 40 + 25 = 45$ m.
blocks.a: Lands after $5$ s; maximum height $45$ m.

blocks.title: Fencing
blocks.q: With $80$ m of fence along three sides of a pen against a wall, what is the largest area?
steps: Sides touching the wall: $x$ each; the side opposite the wall: $80 - 2x$. Area $A = x(80 - 2x)$.
Zeros at $x = 0$ and $x = 40$, so the vertex is at $x = 20$.

blocks.html: Reporting both roots in a time problem, including a negative time. The equation does not know about the story; you do. A launch happens at $t = 0$, so negative times are not part of the answer. Check each root against the situation.
